analysis.title: Stocks Shrug Off AAPL Angst; Dollar Up, Bonds Down Into 'Dem Sweep' Midterms
key_insights: Stronger-than-expected macro (JOLTS, factory orders) pushed Citi's US macro surprise index to its highest level of the year and lifted stocks (AI/Tech led) and bond yields on Nov 3, despite AAPL's overnight disappointment.
The long end underperformed, with yields 2-4bps higher across the curve, as growth hopes dominated inflation fears and heavy corporate supply weighed. The dollar rose and spoiled early gains in gold.

Physical crude collapsed on a supply surge out of the Persian Gulf after Hormuz transit disruptions eased. Forties swung from a nearly $20 premium to a $1.40 discount in three weeks, and Dated Brent plunged.

Brent futures swung more than $6 intraday and settled near $103, as traders parsed conflicting signals on US-Iran peace talks. Iran's Supreme Leader reportedly gave negotiators 'additional authority'.
Combined Saudi, UAE, Iraq and Kuwait exports rose roughly 10% in October to 15.53M bpd, near pre-war levels. Saudi Aramco's CEO said the company will maximize production this quarter.

Diesel prices bounced despite the crude drop, after the New Jersey governor warned port operators against accepting Russian diesel cargoes authorized by the Trump administration. Inventories are low and refining capacity is constrained.

US job openings (JOLTS) hit a four-month high in September with layoffs declining. Traders read this as labor-market resilience that gives the Fed room to raise rates further. The October jobs report is due Friday and is expected to improve from September.

Wednesday's quarterly refunding announcement is the dominant rates focus. Dealers are split on whether Treasury Secretary Bessent will signal a cut in long-end auction sizes. The 10Y stayed below 5.00%.
A divided Congress could offer some relief for the long end, but Mizuho cautioned against chasing that narrative given Trump's willingness to negotiate on spending.

META priced another $15B debt offering with wide initial price talk versus its secondary bonds, implying large new-issue concessions. Higher yields and wider spreads have raised borrowing costs for all AI issuers. Hyperscaler CDS fell notably, while data-center CDS was flat near record highs.

NDX outperformed and bounced after falling over 6% in three days, the worst slide since Liberation Day. QQQ bounced off its 200DMA. The Dow ended red, breadth was weak, and Mag7 beat the SPX 493 for the first time in 4 days.
KOSPI had its first 'death cross' since Oct 2024, when the index fell 12% in 2 months.

Goldman's trading desk rated activity '4 out of 10' with an even buy/sell skew. TMT was sold for a 4th straight session, and HFs were shorting into AI strength with 62% of sales being shorts (above 60% is high). Long-only funds were still sellers.
NeoClouds led the AI rebound, up almost 6%. High Beta 12-Month Winners bounced after a 27% pullback over the last month. Software lagged semis, and homebuilders fell as the 10Y rose.
Gold held $3900 support, and its decoupling from falling real yields suggests liquidation. Bitcoin bounced on chatter that Binance outflows have slowed or stopped.

Prediction markets price a Democratic sweep in the midterms, with the House at 94%. JPMorgan says this is not good for the market. Historically, the S&P 500 median return is 0% from early August to Election Day and 6% in the 3 months after, across 13 midterm years since 1974.

tension_points.bull_case: Midterms are historically a clearing event, with a median S&P 500 return of 6% in the 3 months after Election Day versus 0% from August to Election Day across 13 midterm years since 1974.
tension_points.bear_case: JPMorgan says a Democratic sweep is not great for the market, and Wall Street's cheat sheet calls the likeliest outcome the worst for stocks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Democratic sweep with Trump vowing to veto everything would undercut the clearing-event pattern.

tension_points.bull_case: A reduction in long-end auction sizes at Wednesday's refunding, or a divided Congress, could relieve the long end.
tension_points.bear_case: Heavy corporate supply such as META's $15B offering and Trump's willingness to negotiate on spending (per Mizuho) keep pressure on long-end yields.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wednesday's quarterly refunding announcement not signaling a cut in long-end auction sizes.
